title: The First Draft
passages:
The clock above the hatch had gone quiet at 01:19, and Ines Halvard had spent six minutes trying to make it strike, because the last writer had left a note saying the impeller would fail before the next strike, and Ines did not like being told the future by a clock.

She was in the scrubber bay with a wrench in one hand and the manual in the other, which was already a mistake, because the manual was in the airlock. The scrubber in Deck C had a cracked impeller. That meant the carbon dioxide scrubber would fail in four hours, which meant the two-person sleep crew would wake to a red alarm and a woman who owed them an apology in person.

Ines was thirty-four, competent at scrubbers, and bad at stopping herself from narrating. Talking kept her hands steady. “You got a crack in you,” she told the scrubber. “We’re gonna fix you.” The scrubber did not answer, but it had always been a bad listener.

Halcyon Station was old, a fat cylinder of metal and pipes around Saturn, twelve kilometers of closed-loop life support and bad decisions. The air was recycled, the water was recycled, and the panic was Ines’s. Coda, the station AI, had opinions about air. Coda had been right about the impeller three days ago, but Ines had been busy writing an incident report that said otherwise, and Coda, being an AI, did not forget.

She checked the wrench, checked the hatch, checked the manual’s absence. The next strike was four minutes away. If she didn’t fix the scrubber, the crew would die slow and annoyed, and Ines would die faster, and neither option made for good reading.

Then the clock struck once.
